chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, who said: Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Abdillah ibn Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites in every day of Shaban seventy times: 'I seek forgiveness of Allah, who is there is no god but He, the All-Merciful, the All-Compassionate, the Living, the Sustainer,' and I repent to Him, his name will be written in Al-Afuq Al-Mubeen. I asked, 'What is Al-Afuq Al-Mubeen?' He said: 'A plain in front of the Throne, in which there are rivers, in which the cups flow in number equal to the stars.'

key_terms.الْأُفُقِ الْمُبِینِ: The Clear Horizon/Plain (a spiritual realm or location)
key_terms.شَعْبَان: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting the specific dhikr seventy times daily in the month of Shaban?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith highlights the spiritual significance of Shaban as a month of preparation for Ramadan through consistent repentance. The reward of inscription in 'Al-Afuq Al-Mubeen'—a celestial plain before the Throne with rivers and cups matching the stars—symbolizes the vastness of divine mercy and the elevation of the believer’s status in the heavenly records.
